Lean.ConstantInfo.levelParams.fullDefinition: def levelParams (d : ConstantInfo) : List Name :=   d.toConstantVal.levelParams
Lean.ConstantInfo.levelParams.description: A function that extracts the level parameters associated with a given constant's information.

Lean.ConstantInfo.type.description: A function that retrieves the type expression corresponding to a given constant's information.

Lean.ConstantInfo.hasValue.fullDefinition: def hasValue : ConstantInfo → Bool   | defnInfo _ => true   | thmInfo  _ => true   | _                         => false
Lean.ConstantInfo.hasValue.description: A function that determines whether a given constant's information has an associated value.

Lean.ConstantInfo.defnInfo.description: A function that converts a definition value into its associated constant information.

Lean.ConstantInfo.thmInfo.description: A function that produces the constant information associated with a given theorem value.

Lean.ConstantInfo.axiomInfo.description: A function that retrieves the constant information related to a specified axiom value.

Lean.ConstantInfo.opaqueInfo.description: A function that obtains the constant information associated with a given opaque value.

Lean.ConstantInfo.quotInfo.description: A function that provides the constant information associated with a given quotient value.

Lean.ConstantInfo.inductInfo.description: A function that provides the constant information associated with a specific inductive value.

Lean.ConstantInfo.ctorInfo.description: A function that generates the constant information related to a specified constructor value.

Lean.ConstantInfo.recInfo.description: A function that provides the constant information for a specified recursor value.

Lean.ConstantInfo.toConstantVal.fullDefinition: def toConstantVal : ConstantInfo → ConstantVal   | defnInfo     {toConstantVal := d, ..} => d   | axiomInfo    {toConstantVal := d, ..} => d   | thmInfo      {toConstantVal := d, ..} => d   | opaqueInfo   {toConstantVal := d, ..} => d   | quotInfo     {toConstantVal := d, ..} => d   | inductInfo   {toConstantVal := d, ..} => d   | ctorInfo     {toConstantVal := d, ..} => d   | recInfo      {toConstantVal := d, ..} => d
Lean.ConstantInfo.toConstantVal.description: A function that converts a given constant's information into its corresponding constant value.

Lean.DefinitionVal.toConstantVal.description: A function that converts a given definition value into a corresponding constant value.

Lean.TheoremVal.toConstantVal.description: A function that converts a theorem value into its corresponding constant value.

Lean.OpaqueVal.toConstantVal.description: A function that converts an opaque value into its corresponding constant value.

Lean.ConstantVal.type.description: A function that retrieves the expression type associated with a given constant value.

Lean.DefinitionSafety.unsafe.description: A definition that indicates a state of being unsafe in the context of definition safety.

Lean.DefinitionSafety.partial.description: A statement asserting the concept of partial definition safety within a specified framework.

Lean.DefinitionSafety.safe.description: A definition that indicates the safety status of a mathematical definition.

Lean.Declaration.defnDecl.description: A function that retrieves the declaration associated with a given definition value.

Lean.Declaration.mutualDefnDecl.description: A function that creates a declaration from a list of definitions that are mutually dependent.

Lean.ConstantVal.name.fullDefinition: name : Name   levelParams : List Name   type : Expr   deriving Inhabited, BEq
Lean.ConstantVal.name.description: A function that retrieves the name associated with a specified constant value.

Lean.ConstantVal.levelParams.fullDefinition: levelParams : List Name   type : Expr   deriving Inhabited, BEq
Lean.ConstantVal.levelParams.description: A function that retrieves the list of level parameters associated with a given constant value.

Lean.DefinitionVal.value.fullDefinition: value  : Expr   hints  : ReducibilityHints   safety : DefinitionSafety   /--     List of all (including this one) declarations in the same mutual block.     Note that this information is not used by the kernel, and is only used     to save the information provided by the user when using mutual blocks.     Recall that the Lean kernel does not support recursive definitions and they     are compiled using recursors and `WellFounded.fix`.   -/   all : List Name := [name]   deriving Inhabited, BEq
Lean.DefinitionVal.value.description: A function that retrieves the expression value associated with a given definition value.

Lean.Declaration.thmDecl.description: A function that returns the declaration associated with a given theorem value.

Lean.DefinitionVal.hints.fullDefinition: hints  : ReducibilityHints   safety : DefinitionSafety   /--     List of all (including this one) declarations in the same mutual block.     Note that this information is not used by the kernel, and is only used     to save the information provided by the user when using mutual blocks.     Recall that the Lean kernel does not support recursive definitions and they     are compiled using recursors and `WellFounded.fix`.   -/   all : List Name := [name]   deriving Inhabited, BEq
Lean.DefinitionVal.hints.description: A function that retrieves the reducibility hints associated with a given definition value.

Lean.DefinitionVal.safety.fullDefinition: safety : DefinitionSafety   /--     List of all (including this one) declarations in the same mutual block.     Note that this information is not used by the kernel, and is only used     to save the information provided by the user when using mutual blocks.     Recall that the Lean kernel does not support recursive definitions and they     are compiled using recursors and `WellFounded.fix`.   -/   all : List Name := [name]   deriving Inhabited, BEq
Lean.DefinitionVal.safety.description: A function that determines the safety properties of a given definition value.

Lean.ReducibilityHints.abbrev.description: A definition that refers to an abbreviation of reducibility hints.

Lean.ReducibilityHints.opaque.description: A constant that represents opaque reducibility hints in the system.

Lean.RecursorVal.getFirstMinorIdx.fullDefinition: def RecursorVal.getFirstMinorIdx (v : RecursorVal) : Nat :=   v.numParams + v.numMotives
Lean.RecursorVal.getFirstMinorIdx.description: A function that retrieves the index of the first minor component associated with a given recursor value.

Lean.RecursorVal.getMajorIdx.fullDefinition: def RecursorVal.getMajorIdx (v : RecursorVal) : Nat :=   v.numParams + v.numMotives + v.numMinors + v.numIndices
Lean.RecursorVal.getMajorIdx.description: A function that retrieves the major index associated with a specified recursor value.

Lean.mkRecName.fullDefinition: def mkRecName (declName : Name) : Name :=   Name.mkStr declName "rec"
Lean.mkRecName.description: A function that creates a recursive name based on a given declaration name.

Lean.RecursorVal.numMotives.fullDefinition: numMotives : Nat   /-- Number of minor premises -/   numMinors : Nat   /-- A reduction for each Constructor -/   rules : List RecursorRule   /-- It supports K-like reduction.   A recursor is said to support K-like reduction if one can assume it behaves   like `Eq` under axiom `K` --- that is, it has one constructor, the constructor has 0 arguments,   and it is an inductive predicate (ie, it lives in Prop).
Lean.RecursorVal.numMotives.description: A function that returns the number of motives associated with a given recursor value.

Lean.DefinitionVal.all.comment:
List of all (including this one) declarations in the same mutual block.
Note that this information is not used by the kernel, and is only used
to save the information provided by the user when using mutual blocks.
Recall that the Lean kernel does not support recursive definitions and they
are compiled using recursors and `WellFounded.fix`.
Lean.DefinitionVal.all.fullDefinition: all : List Name := [name]   deriving Inhabited, BEq
Lean.DefinitionVal.all.description: A function that retrieves a list of all declarations included in the same mutual block as a given definition value.

Lean.RecursorVal.all.comment: List of all inductive datatypes in the mutual declaration that generated this recursor
Lean.RecursorVal.all.fullDefinition: all : List Name   /-- Number of parameters -/   numParams : Nat   /-- Number of indices -/   numIndices : Nat   /-- Number of motives -/   numMotives : Nat   /-- Number of minor premises -/   numMinors : Nat   /-- A reduction for each Constructor -/   rules : List RecursorRule   /-- It supports K-like reduction.   A recursor is said to support K-like reduction if one can assume it behaves   like `Eq` under axiom `K` --- that is, it has one constructor, the constructor has 0 arguments,   and it is an inductive predicate (ie, it lives in Prop).
Lean.RecursorVal.all.description: A function that returns a list of all inductive datatypes associated with a specified recursor in a mutual declaration.

Lean.InductiveVal.isRec.comment: `true` when recursive (that is, the inductive type appears as an argument in a constructor).
Lean.InductiveVal.isRec.fullDefinition: isRec : Bool   /-- Whether the definition is flagged as unsafe. -/   isUnsafe : Bool   /-- An inductive type is called reflexive if it has at least one constructor that takes as an argument a function returning the   same type we are defining.   Consider the type:   ```   inductive WideTree where   | branch: (Nat -> WideTree) -> WideTree   | leaf: WideTree   ```   this is reflexive due to the presence of the `branch : (Nat -> WideTree) -> WideTree` constructor.
Lean.InductiveVal.isRec.description: A function that checks if an inductive value is recursive, indicating if the type is used as an argument in one of its constructors.

Lean.InductiveVal.numCtors.description: A function that returns the number of constructors associated with a given inductive value.

Lean.InductiveVal.numIndices.comment:
Number of indices. An index is an argument that varies over constructors.

An example of this is the `n : Nat` argument in the vector constructor `cons : α → Vector α n → Vector α (n+1)`.
Lean.InductiveVal.numIndices.fullDefinition: numIndices : Nat   /-- List of all (including this one) inductive datatypes in the mutual declaration containing this one -/   all : List Name   /-- List of the names of the constructors for this inductive datatype. -/   ctors : List Name   /-- `true` when recursive (that is, the inductive type appears as an argument in a constructor). -/   isRec : Bool   /-- Whether the definition is flagged as unsafe. -/   isUnsafe : Bool   /-- An inductive type is called reflexive if it has at least one constructor that takes as an argument a function returning the   same type we are defining.   Consider the type:   ```   inductive WideTree where   | branch: (Nat -> WideTree) -> WideTree   | leaf: WideTree   ```   this is reflexive due to the presence of the `branch : (Nat -> WideTree) -> WideTree` constructor.
Lean.InductiveVal.numIndices.description: A function that returns the number of indices associated with a given inductive type, where an index represents a variable argument across its constructors.

Lean.InductiveVal.all.comment: List of all (including this one) inductive datatypes in the mutual declaration containing this one
Lean.InductiveVal.all.fullDefinition: all : List Name   /-- List of the names of the constructors for this inductive datatype. -/   ctors : List Name   /-- `true` when recursive (that is, the inductive type appears as an argument in a constructor). -/   isRec : Bool   /-- Whether the definition is flagged as unsafe. -/   isUnsafe : Bool   /-- An inductive type is called reflexive if it has at least one constructor that takes as an argument a function returning the   same type we are defining.   Consider the type:   ```   inductive WideTree where   | branch: (Nat -> WideTree) -> WideTree   | leaf: WideTree   ```   this is reflexive due to the presence of the `branch : (Nat -> WideTree) -> WideTree` constructor.
Lean.InductiveVal.all.description: A function that produces a list of all inductive datatypes present in the mutual declaration that contains the specified inductive type.

Lean.RecursorVal.getFirstIndexIdx.fullDefinition: def RecursorVal.getFirstIndexIdx (v : RecursorVal) : Nat :=   v.numParams + v.numMotives + v.numMinors
Lean.RecursorVal.getFirstIndexIdx.description: A function that retrieves the index of the first occurrence of a specific value in a recursive structure.

Lean.RecursorVal.numParams.fullDefinition: numParams : Nat   /-- Number of indices -/   numIndices : Nat   /-- Number of motives -/   numMotives : Nat   /-- Number of minor premises -/   numMinors : Nat   /-- A reduction for each Constructor -/   rules : List RecursorRule   /-- It supports K-like reduction.   A recursor is said to support K-like reduction if one can assume it behaves   like `Eq` under axiom `K` --- that is, it has one constructor, the constructor has 0 arguments,   and it is an inductive predicate (ie, it lives in Prop).
Lean.RecursorVal.numParams.description: A function that determines the number of parameters associated with a recursor value.
